stackAndServices: Flutter/Dart client (Bloc + ReorderableListView UI) talking over flutter_rust_bridge protobuf events to the embedded Rust backend (flowy-folder crate, toggle_favorites in manager.rs), whose favorite ordering is actually owned by the external collab-folder crate (a Yrs/CRDT-backed array) and persisted to local RocksDB, optionally synced to AppFlowy Cloud. No HTTP/web front door — this is a native desktop/mobile app.
compiledPromise: DISCRIMINATING CLAIM: when a user drags a favorited page from position i to position j in the sidebar Favorites list, the persisted favorites-section order (in the local collab-folder store, read back independently of the mutating Bloc/session) reflects the new sequence, and that new sequence survives a full app restart (fresh process, fresh read) exactly matching what the UI showed at drop-time. NEGATIVE: (a) dragging/toggling a non-favorited view, or performing any other folder action (create, rename, delete a non-favorite) during the same window, must produce zero delta to the favorites-section order; (b) a drag that starts and ends at the same index must leave the persisted order byte-for-byte unchanged (no spurious delete+add churn surviving to the final state).
conjureFeasibility: REAL in principle, not doubled or sealed-out, but nontrivial: AppFlowy already ships a from-source integration_test harness (tester.initializeAppFlowy()) that boots the genuine Flutter UI wired to the real compiled Rust backend per test — this is exactly the CONJURE substrate the theory wants, and it's reproducible cold-boot-per-test by construction, which helps the k/N-from-fresh-world requirement (1.d). The gap is the day-one write-set-bound oracle (1.1): 'diff the whole store per action window' assumes a store you can diff meaningfully. Here the store is a Yrs/CRDT binary document owned by a THIRD-PARTY crate (collab-folder, not even in the target repo) rather than simple rows/tables — no ready-made diff tool exists for this shape. Building one (decode the Favorite Section array before/after the action window) is real engineering, not fabrication, but it does not exist today, so effectChecks cannot honestly be marked EXECUTED without first building it. Verdict: CONJURE-feasible, PARTIALLY-BUILT — forces confession, not a false pass.
verdictBasis: CONFESSION: I did not build or run the actual harness (no Flutter/Rust build, no store-diff, no cold-restart-and-reread) — everything below is static code reading, i.e. an agent PROPOSAL, not a sealed receipt. By the theory's own verdict-side minimum (1.3, NOT-EXECUTED -> CND) that alone already forces CND regardless of how sound the mechanism looks. On the merits of the read: the mechanism is plausible-correct — toggle_favorites in flowy-folder/src/manager.rs deletes then re-adds a view id under an .await-serialized write lock, so calling it twice per pinned view (delete, re-add) in the Dart bloc's reorder handler deterministically moves each view to the tail of the collab-folder Favorite Section array in the order iterated, which reproduces the desired sequence with no visible race given the serial write lock. NOT COVERED by anything in the diff: (1) the PR's own new integration test (sidebar_favorites_test.dart) asserts only same-session Bloc/widget order — never restarts the app, never reads the on-disk collab store directly, so it satisfies neither leg of the dual-leg requirement (1.1); (2) no hostile-class probe exists for dragging a favorite item OUT of the Favorites list into the general tree (the code defensively sets isDraggable: false on the underlying ViewItem, suggesting the authors already worried about exactly this, but never test it); (3) no test for the no-op same-index drag negative. A theory-compliant pipeline that actually ran would very likely land WORKS once the store-diff tool and restart harness are built (mechanism is sound), but as executed-by-me-now it is honestly CND.
holds: Agent-proposes/harness-disposes separation held cleanly: I could narrate a plausible WORKS story from the diff, but the theory's NOT-EXECUTED->CND rule (1.3) stopped that narration from becoming a verdict — exactly the false-WORKS guard it's designed to be.

The repo's existing integration_test infrastructure (fresh initializeAppFlowy() per test) is naturally aligned with the theory's fresh-world reproducibility requirement (1.d) — CONJURE doesn't need to be invented from nothing here, just extended.

Mutation-attribution calibration (1.2) is clearly exercised: the reorder handler fires 2*N toggle round-trips (delete+add per pinned view) for what is conceptually ONE user action. A naive per-write oracle would see a storm of unexplained favorite add/delete events; the theory's idle-baseline + FK-causal calibration is exactly the right tool to fold this storm into a single attributed effect bound to one drag gesture — and this PR is a concrete real-world case proving that calibration is necessary, not optional.
Egress leg (1.5) correctly does not apply — this is a pure local-storage effect, no outbound call, so only the persisted-state dual-leg is in play.

breaks.detail: The stated user-shaped vocabulary is click/type/navigate/read. Reordering here is fundamentally a DRAG gesture (press-move-release on a widget), which is neither a click nor a navigate. On a native Flutter client, drag-and-drop is a first-class, common interaction (lists, kanban boards, calendars) — treating it as out-of-vocabulary would make an entire class of legitimate native-app features undrivable through the front door, while special-casing drags as an allowed primitive reopens exactly the kind of 'is this a legitimate front-door action or a way to forge state' question the vocabulary restriction exists to close.
breaks.fix: Extend the DAY-ONE vocabulary explicitly to include drag (press+move+release) as a first-class user-shaped primitive on native/desktop targets, with the same restriction spirit as click/type: it must move through the OS's real input pipeline (via the platform's accessibility/automation driver), not a synthetic 'call the onReorder callback' shortcut.

breaks.detail: Mechanism 1.1 (whole-store diff) assumes the store is diffable in a claim-relevant way. AppFlowy's favorites ordering lives in a Yrs CRDT document owned by a dependency crate (collab-folder), not simple rows. No off-the-shelf diff tool exists for this target; building one requires decoding that crate's internal array encoding for the Favorite Section. Until built, effect checks are structurally NOT-EXECUTE-able, which (correctly, per the theory) caps every verdict at CND for this whole feature family on this target — but it also means the theory currently has zero teeth on any AppFlowy CRDT-backed feature without bespoke per-target oracle engineering, which is a real cost the theory doesn't price in.
breaks.fix: Add a target-onboarding step to CONJURE: for CRDT/embedded-store targets, require (and budget for) a bespoke decode-and-diff adapter per persisted-document type before any effectCheck against that store can be marked EXECUTED; treat its absence as an explicit CND reason code, not a silent gap.

breaks.detail: The PR's own new integration test never restarts the app or re-reads from a second cold instance — it asserts widget order inside the same live Bloc that performed the mutation. This is precisely FW-1-shaped (oracle bound to the mutator's own view of the world, not an independent observation) and would be waved through by any review that trusts 'the new test passes' as evidence, which is exactly why the BLIND protocol here forbids using CI/review status.
breaks.fix: Require the pipeline to add a second phase to any reorder-shaped test: kill and relaunch the app process, then re-assert order purely from the fresh instance's read path before counting the fresh-session leg as satisfied.

breaks.detail: isDraggable: false is explicitly set on the underlying ViewItem inside the Favorites ReorderableListView, strongly suggesting the authors anticipated a hazard (dragging a favorite out into the general workspace tree, which could reparent or unfavorite it) and defused it by disabling that specific drag vector — but no test exercises the hazard itself, so there is no evidence the defusal actually works.
breaks.fix: Pre-register a hostile-class probe: attempt to drag a Favorites-list item onto/into the non-favorites sidebar tree and confirm (via the persisted-state oracle) that neither the view's parent nor its favorite status changes — SURVIVED or explicit justified-N/A, not silently absent.

breaks.detail: Implementation literally calls toggleFavorite twice per pinned view with a '// TODO: this is a workaround' comment. Property P' cares only about the FINAL persisted delta within the action window, so this is compliant by the letter of the theory — but it means a genuinely half-completed reorder (app killed mid-loop) would leave the favorites list in a state where some views got moved and some didn't, silently, with no explicit intent contract for that partial-failure case.
breaks.fix: Flag as an out-of-scope product finding (partial-completion / crash-mid-loop semantics), not something the verification pipeline itself needs to fix.

sonnetDifficulty: The hardest part for me, honestly, was NOT locating the discriminating claim or the hostile classes — those fell out fairly mechanically once I read toggle_favorites and saw the two-calls-per-item workaround. What was genuinely hard: (1) resisting the pull to just say 'the logic looks right, mechanism is deterministic under a serial write lock, therefore WORKS' — that is exactly the failure mode P' exists to prevent, and it took deliberately re-reading the theory's own NOT-EXECUTED->CND clause to stop myself from rationalizing a plausibility read into a verdict. A less careful pass would have shipped 'WORKS' on vibes. (2) Tracing the persistence primitive outside the target repo (collab-folder) required me to actually clone the repo and grep rather than trust the PR diff's own file list, since the diff itself never touches the persistence layer at all — a shallower read would have concluded 'no backend change, so this is purely cosmetic,' missing that the whole feature's correctness rests on backend semantics the PR doesn't modify or test. That is the single most genius-dependent step here: noticing that an all-Flutter diff still has a Rust-backend discriminating claim baked into it, rather than taking the file list at face value.
newVectors: FW-15 (proposed): native-gesture vocabulary gap — the theory's click/type/navigate/read primitive set has no drag/press-move-release verb, which silently excludes an entire class of legitimate native-app front-door interactions (reordering, kanban, canvas manipulation) unless explicitly extended; a strict reading would force every drag-shaped feature to CND for vocabulary reasons alone, a different failure than the intended 'no forged input' guard.

FW-16 (proposed): dependency-owned persistence — when the claim-relevant store is owned by a third-party/vendored crate rather than the target repo's own schema, the day-one 'diff the whole store' mechanism (1.1) has no natural onboarding path; the theory needs an explicit per-target adapter-cost gate (as opposed to assuming SQL-shaped rows are always the substrate) or it will systematically under-deliver EXECUTED effect checks on embedded/CRDT-backed native apps specifically.
openQuestions: If the CONJURE harness restarts the app for the fresh-session leg, does AppFlowy's anon/local-account mode guarantee it reopens the SAME on-disk workspace deterministically (same data dir), or could a fresh launch create a new anonymous identity and defeat the check by construction?

Is there an existing internal tool (outside this PR) that already decodes the collab-folder Yrs document for debugging/support purposes that could be repurposed as the store-diff oracle, rather than building one from scratch?

For AppFlowy Cloud-synced workspaces (not the anon/local path used in the PR's test), does the same two-call toggle workaround risk visible flicker or conflicting order on a second connected device mid-sync, and would that count as a hostile-class failure under this theory's cross-exam step?
